Be part of a company that’s in the action!

Integra Water Treatment Solutions is a national, Australian owned company who specialize in commercial and industrial water treatment.  Our company has grown from humble beginnings in 1990 to now including 200 plus in our team Australia wide. Our Sydney operation is currently seeking expand the team with a motivated and enthusiastic person to be included our small but experienced team, specialising in water & wastewater treatment, reuse and environmental treatment systems & applications.  

Integra offer expertise in the following areas:
•	Cooling water treatment and tower cleaning
•	Boiler water treatment
•	Pre-treatment, filtration and desalination
•	Waste water treatment
•	Equipment design, repair and installation
•	Cleaning and hygiene solutions


Water & Wastewater Operations: Environmental Consultant 
To be successful in this role you will have experience in working in a team, have good interpersonal and communication skills and be self-motivated. You will have had experience with meeting scheduled customer wastewater service requirements and co-ordinating multiple and competing requirements to limited time frames.

Role Description:
•	Designing strategic environmental action plans to guide sustainable water and wastewater management across Integra Water's industrial, commercial and manufacturing client sites, identifying immediate priorities and establishing long-term treatment and compliance objectives. 
•	Monitoring compliance with environmental statutes and discharge regulations governing water treatment, effluent release and re-use, and initiating corrective measures to protect waterways and surrounding ecosystems. 
•	Conducting comprehensive site assessments prior to the installation or upgrade of water treatment, filtration and wastewater infrastructure to anticipate ecological and regulatory consequences. 
•	Recommending mitigation strategies to offset the environmental impact of industrial water use and effluent discharge, and to support restoration of affected water systems.

•	Coordinating environmental initiatives across client facilities — including manufacturing plants, food processors and commercial premises — to protect water quality and support sustainable resource use. 
•	Compiling environmental data and technical resource inventories to support Integra Water's clients in land-use, treatment infrastructure and resource management decisions.

Requirements: 
•	Relevant Qualification
•	At least 3 years of experience
•	Strong understanding of water and wastewater treatment processes, data evaluation and compliance
•	Effective communicator, able to engage with clients and internal stakeholders across technical and non-technical levels

Full-time

The company

As part of the well-respected and successful international Premier Tech group, and with an
Australian history dating back to the 1950’s, we are a leader within the bulk handling and
packaging equipment industry in Australia.  We are collaborative and innovative, and we love
what we do.

The role

As part of a national team of field service technicians servicing and commissioning a range of
specialised flexible packaging machinery installed around the country and abroad, you will
travel extensively (approx. 75% of the role) throughout metro and regional VIC, as well as
interstate and the occasional international trip. 

Providing expert advice and service for robotic and conventional palletisers, bagging
machines, wrapping and hooding machines and their corresponding control systems, you
should expect to spend most of your time working on customer sites, with the remaining time
spent working between the West Heidelberg office and home.


JOB DESCRIPTION


Fundamental Duties and responsibilities 	

Perform in-house and on-site equipment installations and start-ups  
•	Install equipment at customers’ locations according to safety standards and established corporate procedures 
•	Perform initial start-ups for installed equipment
•	Test and verify installed equipment at customers’ locations
•	Perform tests and verify the proper functioning of equipment
•	Train customers on the proper operation of the equipment
•	Prepare reports on completed installations
•	Do in-house equipment start-ups before it leaves for customers’ locations

Solve various equipment problems for customers
•	Visit customers in order to diagnose equipment problems
•	Find solutions in collaboration with the engineering team
•	Adjust and repair customers’ equipment and ensure it is operated safely and according to the original specifications
•	Prepare reports following service calls
•	Contribute to product development

Do preventive equipment maintenance at various customers’ locations
•	Evaluate the safety, general state and compliance of various equipment
•	Do preventive maintenance and repair on equipment
•	Ensure proper equipment functioning following maintenance visits
•	Plan following maintenance visits as needed
•	Provide on-site and/or remote technical support to clients
•	Prepare reports on the work performed

Provide over the phone technical support for customers 
•	Diagnose problems and identify possible solutions for customers
•	Help customers find safe solutions to problems
•	Promote preventive maintenance and training services to customers

Other generic tasks as required
•	Preparing drawings, plans and designs for mechanical engineering work under the direction of Mechanical Engineers and Engineering Technologists
•	Assisting Mechanical Engineers and Engineering Technologists in the design of mechanical equipment and plant
•	Selecting tools and equipment
•	Assembling and installing new and modified mechanical assemblies, components, machine tools and controls, and hydraulic power systems
•	Estimating material costs and quantities, and machine requirements
•	Performing and directing field and laboratory tests
•	Collecting and analysing data, carrying out complex computations and preparing diagrams
•	Organising and supervising inspection and maintenance of machines and plant
•	Ensuring that designs and finished work are within specifications, regulations and contract provisions
•	Prepares detailed drawings and plans of mechanical engineering work in support of Mechanical Engineers and Engineering Technologists.
 


Advanced Duties and responsibilities 	

•	Assume responsibility for a certain type of service or equipment for customers
•	Do relatively complex installations at customers’ locations
•	Solve complex equipment problems for customers 
•	Provide over the phone technical support for customers 
•	Master preventive maintenance of equipment and suggest improvements to customers during service calls
•	Meet the demand for technical information from potential customers and promote Premier Tech products to customers 


•	Expert Duties and responsibilities 	

•	Be the go-to person for the team as work is carried out
•	Be an instructor and mentor for new team members
•	Collaborate in the equipment design process with the engineering team 
•	Help develop and implement work procedures and methods 
•	Organize installations or repair work to be done
•	Develop and provide specific technical service expertise to the team 
•	Apply different analysis and problem solving skills to diagnose and repair a variety of equipment  
•	Resolve unusual, major and complex problems on customers’ equipment
•	Do major and non-standard equipment installations at customers’ sites




 
COMPETENCIES PROFILE

Qualifications

At least a trade qualification, associate diploma in engineering or suitable equivalent mechanical/electrical/electronic/control automation qualification.

Technical competencies 	

•	In-depth specific knowledge of Premier Tech packaging machinery including Bottom-Up Filling Technology is highly desirable.
•	Interpreting mechanical and general assembly drawings
•	Interpreting hydraulic circuit drawings
•	Interpreting pneumatic circuit drawings
•	Interpreting electrical schematics
•	Interpreting general installation and industrial buildings layouts
•	Industrial PLC, networks and communication protocols

•	Installation, commissioning and troubleshooting of field devices and instrumentation
•	Installation and commissioning of industrial machinery safety systems and guarding.

The restaurant operates lunch and dinner services and provides a diverse menu featuring contemporary Australian cuisine complemented by selected international influences, with a strong emphasis on freshly prepared meals, premium ingredients, and consistent food quality.
The commercial kitchen prepares a broad range of freshly cooked dishes including premium meat, poultry, seafood, pasta, salad, and seasonal menu offerings. Kitchen operations involve coordinated food preparation, commercial cooking, stock management, quality control, and efficient service delivery to meet varying customer demand during lunch, dinner, weekends, and peak trading periods.
Oliver Street Kitchen is committed to maintaining high culinary standards through established kitchen procedures, continuous quality improvement, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Oliver Street Kitchen has an opportunity available for an experienced Cook to join its kitchen team on a full-time basis.
This is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting a broad range of contemporary Australian and internationally inspired dishes in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements. The successful candidate will contribute to all aspects of kitchen operations, including food preparation, cooking, plating, stock control, and maintaining a safe and efficient commercial kitchen environment.
The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, coordinate workflow during busy lunch and dinner service periods, maintain consistency in food quality and presentation, and work collaboratively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to ensure efficient service delivery and a high standard of customer satisfaction.
This is a full-time permanent position based on a minimum 38-hour working week.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Food Preparation and Cooking
• Prepare, cook, and present a wide range of contemporary Australian and internationally inspired dishes in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
• Prepare premium meat, poultry, seafood, pasta, salad, and seasonal menu items using appropriate commercial cooking techniques including grilling, roasting, frying, baking, poaching, braising, and sautéing.
• Undertake ingredient preparation including washing, cutting, trimming, portioning, marinating, and mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
• Monitor cooking times, temperatures, seasoning, and presentation to ensure consistency and quality across all dishes.
• Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service demands, dietary requirements, and customer requests.

Kitchen Operations and Service Delivery
• Support efficient kitchen workflow during lunch and dinner service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
• Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations remain organised, clean, and service-ready throughout each shift.
• Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support coordinated service delivery and order accuracy.
• Assist with the preparation and execution of daily specials and seasonal menu offerings.
• Adapt efficiently to changing service demands while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

Stock Control and Kitchen Organisation
• Assist with receiving, inspecting, storing, and rotating food supplies in accordance with established stock control procedures.
• Apply FIFO stock rotation principles to minimise spoilage and maintain product freshness.
• Monitor stock usage and advise senior kitchen staff of inventory shortages or ordering requirements.
• Participate in stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
• Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety requirements.

Food Safety and Compliance
• Maintain compliance with Australian Food Safety Standards and safe food handling practices.
• Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness throughout food preparation areas, equipment, utensils, and workstations.
• Monitor food storage, preparation, cooking, cooling, and holding temperatures to ensure regulatory compliance.
• Follow workplace food safety procedures and cleaning schedules to maintain a safe commercial kitchen environment.
• Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation and maintenance of commercial kitchen equipment.

General Duties and Team Contribution
• Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
• Work collaboratively with kitchen staff and management to support efficient daily operations.
• Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive team-oriented approach.
• Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff with accuracy and attention to detail.
• Participate in ongoing workplace training and continuous professional development to further culinary skills and operational knowledge.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
• Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, together with at least one (1) year of relevant full-time experience in a commercial kitchen; or equivalent skills and experience suitable for the position.
• Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking meals within a commercial restaurant, hospitality, or food service environment.
• Sound knowledge of Australian Food Safety Standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
• Ability to prepare and cook a diverse range of contemporary Australian cuisine using a variety of commercial cooking techniques.
• Experience working efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
• Availability to work weekends, evenings, public holidays, and rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
• Technical commercial cookery skills.
• Contemporary Australian cuisine preparation.
• Food preparation, cooking, and presentation.
• Time management and organisational skills.
• Kitchen workflow and service coordination.
• Attention to detail and quality control.
• Communication and teamwork.
• Problem-solving and adaptability.
• Food safety and regulatory compliance.
• Commitment to continuous improvement and professional standards.

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant qualifications, experience, and availability.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

The Client  

Cars 4 All Pty Ltd is an automotive service and repair workshop based in Brooklyn, VIC, specialising in vehicle diagnostics, mechanical repairs, and routine servicing.  

They are seeking two (2) experienced Motor Mechanics to join their team in Brooklyn, VIC. 

 

 

The Role 

The Motor Mechanic is responsible for delivering diagnostic, repair, and maintenance services across a range of vehicles, ensuring all work meets technical specifications, safety standards, and customer requirements. 

This is for two (2) full-time positions with an annual salary set at $80,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation.  

 

The Responsibilities 

Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults using diagnostic tools, testing equipment, and technical procedures 

Inspect vehicles and assess system performance across engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, and braking systems 

Perform servicing and maintenance tasks including oil changes, brake servicing, and system adjustments 

Dismantle, repair, and reassemble engine components, transmissions, and associated mechanical systems 

Replace defective parts and components in accordance with manufacturer specifications and repair standards 

Conduct testing and verification of repairs to ensure functionality, safety, and compliance 

Interpret technical manuals, service documentation, and repair guides to support accurate diagnostics and repairs 

Maintain records of servicing, repairs, and parts usage in line with workshop and compliance requirements 

Identify additional faults or service requirements and communicate findings to supervisors or customers 

Ensure all work is completed in accordance with workplace safety procedures and automotive standards 

Maintain workshop tools, equipment, and work areas in safe and operational condition 

Coordinate with team members to ensure efficient workflow and timely completion of jobs 

 

 

The Requirements:	 

Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology or equivalent qualification 

Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis and/or Diploma of Automotive Technology highly regarded.  

At least 2 years of motor mechanical experience in a commercial workshop setting 

At least 2 years’ experience diagnosing mechanical and electrical faults across vehicle systems 

Minimum 2 years’ using OBD-II diagnostic tools, workshop equipment and vehicle service information. 

Minimum 2 years’ experience performing servicing, maintenance, and repair of engines, transmissions, and braking systems 

Must have at least 2 years experience working with Asian and European car vehicles 

Must have at least 2 years motor mechanical experience with AWDs, 4WDs, 

Must have at least 2 years experience with Hybrid vehicles 

Ability to interpret technical manuals, specifications, and repair documentation 

Strong problem-solving skills and ability to identify and resolve mechanical issues efficiently 

Good understanding of workplace safety procedures and automotive compliance standards 

Ability to work independently and manage workload in a workshop environment 

Good communication skills and ability to liaise with team members and customers 

Valid Driver’s Licence
